_why: ⏱ 2026-09-27 · LEAD RULING SHIELD-R3, row O-BOXES-UNSHIELDED-FROM-SPIKES. THE PER-IP LIMIT ON THE CREDENTIAL
ENDPOINTS, AS CODE. services/edge-shield keeps one GLOBAL cap per class and never reads the client's address
(the ADR no.011 / ADR no.020 posture, held by tooling/ci/assert-glitchtip-no-ip.mjs). The per-IP half lives in
Cloudflare's own rate-limiting rule on the nikatru.com zone instead — the zone's single Free-plan rule, which
until now guarded only GlitchTip's login endpoint and was edited by hand in the dashboard.
This file IS the zone's whole `http_ratelimit` phase: `rules` below is exactly what the phase entrypoint holds.
· APPLIED by .github/workflows/deploy-workers.yml's edge-shield job, after merge, with
`node tooling/ops/edge-ratelimit-rule.mjs --apply` (a PUT of the phase entrypoint, then a re-read that must
equal this file). Never by hand: a dashboard edit is drift, and the next line finds it.
· COMPARED weekly (and on demand) by .github/workflows/ops-watch.yml's edge-shield job, `node tooling/ops/edge-ratelimit-rule.mjs`:
0 the live phase equals this file · 1 it differs (the step names each field) · 2 could not look.
🔴 THE FREE PLAN READS THE PATH AND NOTHING ELSE, AND THAT SHAPES THE RULE. Cloudflare's rate-limiting
availability table (developers.cloudflare.com/waf/rate-limiting-rules, read 2026-09-27): on Free the rule
expression may use `Path` and `Verified Bot` only — no host, no method, no query; the counting characteristic
is the IP (`cf.colo.id` + `ip.src`); the period and the mitigation timeout are 10 s; the action is block; one
rule per zone. So the expression below names PATHS. Both path families are unique to their host on this zone:
`/_allauth/` is GlitchTip's (Box B) and `/auth/v1/` GoTrue's (Box C), and no other nikatru.com host serves
either.
🔴 ⏱ 2026-10-01 · `/auth/v1/token` IS NOW IN THE RULE, with every MFA path under `/auth/v1/factors/` and
`/auth/v1/reauthenticate` (SYN-A2 / PB-01, row O-ONE-CLIENT-CAN-EXHAUST-THE-CREDENTIAL-CAP). Until then no
per-IP limit covered the password grant: one client's junk password posts above 5/s filled the shield's ONE
global credential bucket (300/min per colo), and every sign-up, OTP, recovery, verify and MFA step in that colo
was refused at the shield, before GoTrue's own per-IP limiter could tell that client from anyone else. The
shield now keeps three credential buckets (services/edge-shield/src/classify.ts), and this rule bounds one
address on all three. It is still ONE rule: the Free plan allows one, so the expression is extended.
⚠️ THE REFRESH TRADE-OFF, forced by the plan. The grant lives in the QUERY, which this rule cannot read, so it
counts every `grant_type=refresh_token` call too; Cloudflare's block answers 429; and gotrue-dart 2.26.0 treats
a refresh 4xx as final — it deletes the stored session and emits signedOut (the failure LEAD RULING SHIELD-R2
keeps the shield's own refresh refusal at 503 for). What that costs, read in gotrue-dart 2.26.0
`_refreshAccessToken` and package:retry 3.1.2 `delay()` on 2026-10-01:
· ON AVERAGE, NOTHING BELOW ~1,800 SESSIONS BEHIND ONE ADDRESS. 5 per 10 s is 1,800 an hour, and a session
refreshes about once an hour: the hourly bound GoTrue's own per-IP refresh limit applies (150 per 5 min).
But this rule counts in 10 s windows, not 5 min ones, so a 6th refresh from one address inside any 10 s is
a 429 however few sessions are behind it on average;
· IN AN ORIGIN 5xx (Box C, the tunnel, or the shield's own 503 refresh cap) gotrue-dart re-asks a refresh at
0, 0.4, 1.2, 2.8 and 6.0 s (200 ms × 2^n): FIVE in 10 s, exactly the limit. One session alone stays under
it; a second session refreshing from the same address in those seconds puts the address over, and the
refresh that draws the 429 signs its user out;
· ONE COUNT PER ADDRESS: 5 password, MFA or refresh calls in 10 s from an address 429 every refresh from it
for the 10 s mitigation — behind a shared NAT, other users' refreshes too.
GOTRUE_RATE_LIMIT_HEADER on Box C (ADR no.059 R4-08; unset when last measured, 2026-09-24) gives GoTrue's own
per-IP /token limiter the real address; a plan whose rule reads the query (Pro: Query and Host — a spend,
owner-gated) would let the refresh grant out of this rule.
⚠️ THE RESIDUAL, with the rule in place: a shared GLOBAL bucket is still lockable by about its cap ÷ this
rule's per-IP rate — 300/min ÷ 30/min = 10 addresses at the limit, per colo, per credential class. Ten such
addresses lock one class in one colo; they no longer lock the other two, and one address no longer locks
any. services/edge-shield/test/wrangler-config.test.ts holds every credential cap at that ratio or above.
The threshold and the action are the ones the zone's rule already had (5 requests per 10 s per IP, block for
10 s; the owner-proven GlitchTip login limit). The test clients' peak on these paths, counted from code, is at
most 3 in any 10 s from one address, 4 if two laptop scripts overlap — and that count already included the
password grants (the draft-shield report, e2e runner and laptop), so no test reaches 5. No script in this repo
sends a refresh grant (grep, 2026-10-01); an SDK session in a test run refreshes at most once an hour.
⚠️ NOT VERIFIED BEFORE MERGE: that the deploy token (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) holds Zone → Zone WAF → Edit on
nikatru.com, which the PUT needs, and that the live phase is the one rule this file describes. Neither is
readable from a lane. A missing scope makes the apply step answer HTTP 403 → exit 2, and the edge-shield
deploy job goes red where it happened; the live rule is left exactly as it was (the PUT is all or nothing).

rules.description: nikatru credential endpoints, per IP (tooling/edge-ratelimit-rule.json; LEAD RULING SHIELD-R3)
